pure-announcement.rationale: Beyond the launch framing it explains a transferable federation architecture — one canonical source-of-truth registry with public and private sub-registries built on top — not merely that a product shipped.

duplicate.rationale: None of the nearest concepts cover a canonical-registry-plus-federated-sub-registries pattern; extension-registry-trust is the closest by theme but argues the contrasting position of curated-by-default for unsandboxed extensions, not this registry's open self-report plus reactive moderation model.

unfalsifiable.rationale: Describes an actually-shipped, open-source system with a published OpenAPI spec and a documented moderation policy, independently checkable.

durability.rationale: The source-of-truth-plus-federated-sub-registries pattern, and reactive community moderation as its governance backstop, are architectural choices that outlive this specific preview launch.

actionability.rationale: It shows the shape of a working architecture and the reasoning for federating rather than centralizing everything, but stops short of prescriptive trade-off guidance for someone designing a similar registry.

atomicity.rationale: One coherent idea stateable in a paragraph: a canonical, openly-governed registry as source of truth, with public and private sub-registries layering curation on top, moderated reactively by community flagging.
